title: Part-mesh alias table: topology `part` id -> mesh provenance `part_id`
notes: A topology edge's `part` (docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md's vocabulary, authored per-edge) and an installed mesh's provenance.json `part_id` (the tessellation run's own naming, data/meshes/README.md) are two namespaces with zero exact matches at 2026-09-10. This table is the one sanctioned bridge between them (strategy brief BRIEF_20260909_topology_part_vocabulary_mesh_mapping, option b: declared configuration, never fuzzy matching, never renaming installed meshes).

Every entry asserts 'these two strings name the same physical part' and carries the evidence for that identity -- the mesh's own provenance.json, data/meshes/README.md, or a drawing number. A pair whose identity cannot be evidenced stays out of this table: the annotate app's 'no installed mesh' empty state is the honest answer, never a guessed match.
Values map to a mesh's `part_id`, not its sha256, so a re-tessellated mesh installed under the same part identity keeps its aliases.

rotorkit's assembly_extract_20261001T022446Z (2026-10-01) installed the pitch linkage's remaining parts, and two of them became rows the same day: `hub` and `pitch_arm`, both exact drawing-number matches against one installed solid each. Two did NOT -- `pitch_link`'s body and `blade_root` -- and the reason is not that the meshes are missing: blade 1 carries the INSTRUMENTED variants (546293-002 and 551438-001) where the topology names the design parts (213862-002 and 216332-001), and 216332-001 is installed as two distinct geometries. Which drawing a topology part should name when a test article differs from the design is a decision nobody has made; docs/issues/ISSUE_20260930_blade_1s_pitch_link_is_the_instrumented_546293_002.md and ISSUE_20260930_four_pitch_linkage_alias_rows_wait_on_rotorkits_extraction.md carry it. The same run also re-extracted the pitch-link bearing under a SECOND geometry signature, so this table's `spherical_bearing_pitch_link` row now names one of two identical installed meshes -- ISSUE_20260930_one_solid_two_geometry_signatures_across_two_runs.md.

The eleven `asm217755_*` rows were added by handoff extracted_mesh_alias_rows (2026-09-15) against the piece-part meshes rotorkit's assembly_step_part_extraction (2026-09-14) extracted from `217755-001 A.1 PROPULSION ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW Released.stp` and installed into data/meshes/. Each row is an exact drawing- or spec-number match on both sides, with the mesh side read off the live provenance.json at merge time rather than transcribed. Five further topology part ids stayed OUT at that point, as candidates rather than rows, each needing a decision nothing in the STEP can settle; what each one needed is recorded in docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260915_extracted_mesh_alias_rows.md.

Three of those five candidates were decided by handoff vpa_pitch_linkage_topology_and_feature_fits (2026-09-30), on parts-list evidence that had not been read when they were filed, and became six of the rows below. Candidate 1 (`tan_link_mount_215175_002`, the dash number): 217755-001 A.1's parts list carries BOTH dash numbers, find 41 `215175-001 ... CW` qty 1 and find 73 `215175-002 ... CCW` qty '-', so the CW assembly every mesh here came from contains the -001. Candidate 2 (two `spherical_bearing_*` ids against three MS141xx meshes): 213862-002 A's own parts list is `213861-002` x1 plus `MS14101-3` x2, and the `_815597cb` mesh's two instances both sit under `213862-002.1` -- so that one is the pitch link's, `_34f032f0` (three instances, one per `212956-005`) is the tangential link's, and `MS14103-3` is the tangential link's other end. Candidate 4 (`gas_spring`): see its own row. Candidates 3 (the two `flanged_bushing_*` ids) and 5 (`asm217755_214723_002`, installed with no candidate id) are UNCHANGED and still out, and so is `spherical_bearing_in_vpa` -- which candidate 2's resolution leaves with no mesh at all, since all three MS141xx geometries are now accounted for in the two links and none of them is in the VPA.

Consumed by apps/annotate/commands.js `resolveMeshIdentifier` (exact match, consulted only after a direct sha256/part_id match misses) and, since handoff annotate_affordances_flyout_and_mesh_gating (2026-09-14), by scripts/build_topology_projection.py `resolve_mesh` -- the same precedence in Python, so the topology projection can stamp per-part mesh availability for the viewer to gate its 3D affordances on. Paired against both live vocabularies by tests/test_part_mesh_aliases.py and apps/annotate/run_tests.cjs's [real] tier.

The two rows the 2026-09-30 extraction left undecided -- `pitch_link` and `blade_root` -- were added by handoff kinematic_sweep_animation (2026-10-01) on Jeff's ruling that day: a topology part names the DESIGN, non-instrumented part, and its alias row points at the design-part mesh. Blade 1 carries the instrumented variant of both (546293-002 and 551438-001), so a design mesh drawn at blade 1's occurrence takes its placement from the INSTRUMENTED mesh's provenance -- the design mesh's own instances are the other blades. That substitution is only sound because the design and instrumented meshes share a local frame, which each row records as a measurement rather than an assumption.

The OTHER MS14101-3 geometry, picked by the same instance-path evidence from the other side. Three tangential links, three of these bearings. The two MS14101-3 directories are distinct SOLIDS under one spec number, which is why the store suffixes each with its geometry signature; fitting both reads the same ball radius and the same race-seat radius, as two copies of one catalog part should.

The dash-number question the 2026-09-15 candidate list left open, answered by the assembly's own parts list rather than by a judgement: 217755-001 A.1 (drawing-checker run 20260909_174538, sheet 1) carries find 41 '215175-001 TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW' qty 1 and find 73 '215175-002 TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT ASEMBLY, PROPELLER, CCW' qty '-'. READ THIS BEFORE USING THE ROW: the two dash numbers are the two HANDS of one design, not two revisions of one part, so this alias does not claim they are the same solid. It claims that the tangential link mount of the assembly every mesh in this store came from -- the CW 217755-001 -- is the -001, and that it is the mount the -002 topology part describes, mirrored. A reader looking at this mesh for a CCW build is looking at the mirror image. The mesh is data/meshes/9913d0cff39c81393aad6ff5f1c6e16a472167289ce06398cea84e1709065d6c, product_name '215175-001', 40 solids: the mount INSTALLATION, whose machined detail 215198-001 is installed separately as `asm217755_215198_001` and whose own height 79.00 +/-0.10 is traced to 215198-A sheet 1 (2026-09-10).

So, as with `pitch_link`, the design mesh drawn at blade 1's occurrence takes its placement from the INSTRUMENTED mesh's provenance (`asm217755_551438_001`, instance 211587-001.3 under prd-e-03372837.1, a pure 72 deg rotation about X) and needs no offset.
